key_insight: When LoRA starts with B=0, gradient attribution only searches the B matrix, so a same-pool random mask is a fairer comparison—and it surprisingly yields lower loss-based forgetting than gradient masking.
engineering_relevance: For parameter-efficient continual learning in constitutive modeling and other scientific fine-tuning settings, simpler random parameter selection may preserve prior-task performance better than gradient-based attribution under the tested setup.
method: Compare initialization-time gradient masking vs. uniform random masking
Control for the LoRA pool confound by restricting both methods to the same parameters
Measure backward transfer / forgetting across sequential tasks
evidence_signal: Across seven seeds on Qwen2.5-3B, the same-pool random mask consistently beat gradient attribution on loss-based backward transfer, with the effect driven mostly by the medical task (80% of the aggregate).
watch_item: The result is specific to the tested task order, LoRA B=0 initialization, and model/dataset mix, so it should not be generalized without replication under different adapters and sequences.
paper_title: Static Gradient Attribution Underperforms a Density-Matched Random Mask on Loss-Based Forgetting Within LoRA B-Matrix
